verses.text: "If a man steals an ox or a sheep and kills it or sells it, he must pay back five oxen for the ox, or four sheep for the sheep.
If a thief is caught breaking into a house at night and is hit and killed, the person who killed him is not guilty of murder.

But if it happens after the sun has come up, the person who killed him is guilty of murder. A thief must pay back what he stole. If he has nothing, he must be sold as a slave to pay for what he stole.
If the stolen animal is found alive with him, whether it is an ox, a donkey, or a sheep, he must pay back twice as much.
If a man lets his animals graze in a field or vineyard, and lets them loose so that they eat in someone else's field, he must pay for the loss from the best of his own field or vineyard.
If a fire breaks out and spreads into thorn bushes so that it burns up bundles of grain, or standing grain, or the whole field, the one who started the fire must pay for the loss.
If a man gives his neighbour money or goods to keep safe, and they are stolen from the neighbour's house, the thief, if he is caught, must pay back twice as much.
But if the thief is not found, the owner of the house must go before God, to find out whether he himself has taken his neighbour's goods.

In every case of a dispute over property, whether it is an ox, a donkey, a sheep, clothing, or anything lost, where someone says, 'This is mine,' both people must bring their case before God. The one whom God declares guilty must pay back twice as much to the other.
If a man gives his neighbour a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any other animal to look after, and it dies or is hurt or is taken away while no one is looking,
the neighbour must take an oath before the LORD that he did not take his neighbour's property. The owner must accept this, and no payment is needed.
But if the animal was stolen from the neighbour, he must pay the owner for it.
If it was torn to pieces by a wild animal, he must bring the remains as proof. He does not have to pay for what was torn to pieces.
If a man borrows an animal from his neighbour, and it is hurt or dies while the owner is not there, he must pay for it.
But if the owner was there, the borrower does not have to pay. If the animal was hired, the money paid for the hire covers the loss.
If a man talks a young woman into having sex with him, and she is a virgin who is not promised to be married, he must pay the bride price and marry her.
If her father completely refuses to let him marry her, he must still pay the full bride price that is paid for a virgin.
Do not let a woman who practises witchcraft live.
Anyone who has sex with an animal must be put to death.
Anyone who offers sacrifices to any god other than the LORD must be destroyed.
Do not mistreat or oppress a foreigner, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
Do not take advantage of a widow or an orphan.
If you do, and they cry out to me, I will surely hear their cry.
My anger will burn, and I will kill you with the sword. Then your wives will become widows and your children orphans.
If you lend money to one of my people who is poor, do not treat it like a business deal. Do not charge him interest.
If you take your neighbour's coat as a promise that he will pay you back, give it back to him before the sun goes down,
because that coat is the only covering he has for his body. What else will he sleep in? When he cries out to me, I will hear, because I am kind.
Do not speak evil against God, and do not curse a ruler of your people.
Do not hold back the offerings from your harvest and from your wine and oil. You must give me the firstborn of your sons.
Do the same with your cattle and your sheep. Let them stay with their mothers for seven days, and on the eighth day give them to me.
You are to be my holy people. So do not eat the meat of an animal killed by wild animals in the field. Throw it to the dogs.
